To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
calcium mediated Cyclin D dynamics can extend the oscillatory range and that this may explain the large increase in cortical cell proliferation observed in vivo.
calcium dependent Cycline D dynamics can render cells more susceptible to oscillations and that this may account for a large part of the large increase of proliferation observed experimentally.
(i) calcium accelerates cell cycle progression, but by a small amount only; and that (ii) calcium can recruit quiescent (G0 phase) cells onto the cell-cycle via a stable oscillatory mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the impact that calcium signalling has upon the cell cycle of radial glial cells, and the potential role that calcium may play in the proliferation of cortical progenitors.

the modelling of the coupling between ATP mediated intracellular calcium release, Cyclin D dynamics and cell cycle progression during cortical brain development and suggests that the recruitment of quiescent cells to the cell cycle may account for much of the observed increase in proliferation rates in the presence of ATP mediated calcium release.
understanding how intercellular signalling regulates the proliferation of radial glial cells in the developing brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

calcium dependent signalling is not responsible for the large increase in cell proliferation observed experimentally but rather that calcium signalling is a key component of the mechanism by which quiescent radial glia are recruited onto the cell cycle.
the primary effect of ATP mediated intracellular calcium signals is to recruit cells into the cell cycle, rather than to accelerate the cell cycle.
calcium mediated Cyclin D dynamics can act to both accelerate the cell cycle and also recruit G0 cells onto the cell-cycle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
calcium dependent Cyclins, in particular Cyclin D, may play a key role in the coupling between calcium signalling and cell cycle progression in radial glial cells.

calcium dependent Cyclins, like Cyclin D, are important in regulating cell proliferation and cell cycle entry, and that the coupling between intracelluar calcium and cell cycle dynamics can be used to model and understand how cell populations are controlled.

calcium dependent Cycline D dynamics extend the cell cycle oscillatory region to low Cyclin D synthesis values, and that this can be a mechanism by which quiescent cells are recruited onto the cell cycle and thereby increase proliferation rates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
calcium mediated signalling between glial cells is likely to play a crucial role in cortical development, by regulating the cell cycle of quiescent cells.

a calcium mediated increase in Cyclin D synthesis rate can act to recruit cells onto the cell-cycle and thereby increase overall proliferation, without significantly accelerating the cell cycle itself.

the calcium dependent cell cycle acceleration and the calcium dependent cell recruitment mechanisms are not necessarily mutually exclusive and that both are likely to be important in the context of cortical development.
